Fewer students enrolled in Stokes County's only school district in 2024-25
J. K. Payne
The only school district in Stokes County had declining enrollment in the 2024-25 school year, according to the North Carolina Department of Public Instruction.
There were 5,358 students in Stokes County Schools, 1.5% fewer the year before.
The enrollment numbers in Stokes County fell short of the state's trend, which shows an overall increase in enrollment across North Carolina.
Stokes County Schools has a main office in Danbury and is the only school district within Stokes County.
North Carolina continues to rank near the bottom nationally for public school funding, according to the Education Law Center's 2025 "Making the Grade" report. The report found the state ranked 50th out of 51 states and Washington, D.C., for cost-adjusted per-pupil funding from state and local sources, spending $12,193 per student — about $5,660 below the national average. North Carolina also ranked last among states for funding effort, which measures public school revenue as a share of the state's economic activity.
Teacher attrition remains a concern in North Carolina, though the rate has leveled off since its post-pandemic high, according to the North Carolina Department of Public Instruction. The state’s teacher attrition rate was 10.11% in 2024-25, up from 9.88% the previous year but below the 11.5% rate reported for 2022-23. DPI said attrition was highest among newer teachers and those with 30 or more years of experience, while state leaders pointed to compensation, training and professional support as key issues for strengthening the teaching workforce.
